# Acquired-block Markov feedback: a separately paid planner

Exploratory extension, outside the accepted 18:24 freeze and its review.
The planner is ordinary finite-horizon coarse-MDP dynamic programming. The
question here is whether the acquired certificate actually covers its policy
class, with all additional acquisition paid. No new Bellman algorithm is claimed.

## 1. Exact task/interface

There are m unknown stochastic A_a on n explicitly named states, with the
same ordinary forward generative interface as the accepted source. The task
specifies a fixed initial probability ell and terminal reward b in [0,1]^n.
The acquired partition P=ZW must preserve both, exactly as before.

The output is an OFFLINE policy and value certificate for this explicit-state
simulator. A simulated rollout retains its current microscopic state label i;
querying (a,i) returns the next label. At each remaining horizon t the policy
looks up g=block(i) and a=pi_t(g). Actual deployment does not thereby acquire a
physical sensor, hidden-state estimator or authenticated block observation.
Those would be additional premises/costs, and are not constructed here.

The comparison class is all deterministic time-dependent Markov policies on
the acquired block labels. Randomized Markov block policies can also be
covered by convexity. Arbitrary microscopic feedback and arbitrary
history-dependent block feedback are NOT in this class. Small prediction rank
alone is not a claim that they have no advantage.

## 2. The extra operator family

Let D_g be the diagonal indicator of block g. P,Q commute with every D_g.
For a deterministic map pi:{1,...,r}->{1,...,m}, define

    A_pi = sum_g D_g A_(pi(g)),
    B_pi[g,:] = B_(pi(g))[g,:].

Both matrices are stochastic. A product of the A_pi operators represents a
time-dependent Markov block policy, with the usual backward-value ordering.
There are m^r one-step maps, not m^(rL), but m^r is still exponential in r.
The first historical construction explicitly acquired/checked ALL of them.
The current polynomial sufficient route instead uses the acquired block-norm
comparison in BLOCK_COMPARISON_PROOF.md; it does not claim an optimal norm planner.

# Independent whole review: acquired-block feedback planning

## Verdict

PASS, within the explicit-state, offline, time-dependent acquired-block Markov-policy interface, conditional on the stated fresh iid sampling and independently fresh probe premises. This is a separate review of the feedback extension, not a retroactive enlargement of the open-word receipt.

The final polynomial receiver genuinely reconstructs the local norm certificates, the uniform model-error bound, the exact Bellman policy, and the packed retained interface. No mathematical blocker remains. The code is a typed scientific API with assertions enabled, not a hostile-JSON authentication service. It does not authenticate source truth, independence or sampling chronology. In particular, seeded synthetic observations/probes do not establish those probabilistic premises.

I read the complete final PROOF, BLOCK_COMPARISON_PROOF, SCOPE, README, PRIOR_MATCH_AND_COSTS and all new Python bodies, including the final receiver and the two optional consumers/counterexamples. All 23 branch files and 16 dependencies match the final freeze manifest:

`FEEDBACK_FREEZE_MANIFEST.json`, 8,715 bytes,
SHA-256 `da0208fdba68e98e77da2d4cb25d2e0e5f452928cd7c08554dca213ed7da14fe`.

The exact per-file source binding is reproduced in the appendix. Frozen author sources/results were not modified. Test regeneration wrote to temporary locations or called nonmutating run() entry points.

## 1. Actual feedback operator family

For the block-average projection P=ZW in uniform H=I/n and Q=I-P, each block selector D_g commutes with P and Q. Row selection

    A_pi=sum_g D_g A_(pi(g))

is precisely the backward-value transition operator for a microscopic state whose block determines its current action. It is stochastic. Its coarse row is the corresponding row of the chosen action. Products describe time-dependent Markov feedback on acquired block labels, not arbitrary observation histories.

    ||Q A_pi P x||_H^2

      <=sum_a e_in,a^2 ||x||_H^2.

Thus the implemented sqrt(m) times the maximum incoming bound is safe. The outgoing row and coarse row-error bounds are unchanged, since each row chooses one already controlled action. # Polynomial sufficient residual geometry, actually acquired

Separate unreviewed extension, not in the accepted routing-certificate ZIP.
The inequality below is the standard block-norm comparison/small-gain
argument, not a new principle of matrix analysis. Its role is to replace
explicit m^r policy norm acquisition by paid local observation-derived checks.

Let F_a=Q C_a Q and decompose vectors by acquired blocks. For each source
block g and target block h, acquire a simultaneous upper bound

    u_gh >= max_a ||Q_g C_a[g,h] Q_h||_2,
    Q_g=I_g−1_g 1_g^T/|g|.

The nonnegative r-by-r comparison matrix U=(u_gh) is learned from the data;
its entries or a useful spectral bound are not supplied. For any policy pi
selecting one action per output/source block and any vector x,

    ||(Q C_pi Q x)_g||_2 <= sum_h u_gh ||x_h||_2.

Taking the Euclidean norm of these block norms proves

    max_pi ||Q C_pi Q||_2 <= ||U||_2.

Acquire/check ||U||_2 with an exact small-dimensional PSD norm test. Together
with the simultaneous full-matrix observation event, the true family bound is

    alpha_feedback <= ||U||_2 + sqrt(m)*t.

This can fail even if all actual policies contract: blockwise absolute norms
discard cancellation and alignment. Thus it is a sufficient tractable
certificate, not an algorithm for optimal switched-norm recognition and not
a refutation of the earlier scoped hard certification language.

For unequal block sizes, the executable embeds each rectangular observed
block as the upper-right block of a zero square matrix on |g|+|h| coordinates.
The two-block projection acts by Q_g and Q_h. Its norm is exactly the norm
of Q_g C_a[g,h] Q_h. The inherited count normalizer is corrected by the
known rational factor n*N_block/[(|g|+|h|)*N_coarse]. Zero observed blocks
have exact zero observed norm (their true uncertainty remains in t).

There are m r² local checks with failure delta/(8m r²) each, all using probes
fresh after data/partition selection. This replaces the old norm event in
the final certificate, rather than adding unbudgeted probability. Each
observed nonzero count appears in exactly one block per action, although
each local power iteration revisits it and projections/state work are extra.
The sparse multiply count is O(p*sum_a nnz(C_a)); local state/projection work
is O(p*m*n*r), and there are O(mr²) scalar norm admissions. This is polynomial
